title: Seamless Mass Mailings, Simplified
text:
At TELUS Health / LifeWorks, I have successfully executed dozens of mail merges, many of which had thousands of recipients, a wide variety of templates, tight deadlines, and constant changes to both templates and data. With a natural inclination for process efficiency, I’ve created a Python package to streamline the process.


Features & Benefits

Reliable Mail Merges: Eliminate common errors and inconsistencies that come with manual mail merges.
Effortless Re-runs: Quickly re-run merges with updated data or templates with minimal manual steps.
Dynamic Template Management: Easily handle frequent template updates across multiple campaigns.
Group-Specific Flexibility: Automatically generate the right combination of templates for different recipient groups.
Time-Saving Automation: Reduce repetitive manual steps and free up time for more important work.
Scalable for Complexity: Designed to handle high volumes and complex mailing structures with ease.
Built-in Formatting Tools: Convert numbers into properly formatted currencies, and standardize dates in both English and French.
Address Processing: Clean and structure address fields automatically for mailing accuracy.
Consistent Output: Ensure all merged documents use the same professional, localized formatting—no manual tweaks required.

title: RichText
text:
Example:

“Parts of a string where there are bolded elements and italicized elements.”

Note that RichText ignores styling and uses the default style in the Word template unless explicitly specified.
Use the patched RT class in this module and initialize with a RTFormatOpts instance to set up default styling options.


RTFormatOpts

 RTFormatOpts (style:str=None, color:str=None, highlight:str=None,
               size:int=22, subscript:bool=None, superscript:bool=None,
               bold:bool=False, italic:bool=False, underline:str=False,
               strike:bool=False, font:str='Arial', url_id:str=None)

Default options:
style: str = None  # based on style name in Word doc
color: str = None  # e.g., `#00FFFF`
highlight: str = None  # e.g., `#FFFF00`
size: int = 22  # == 11 in Word 
subscript: bool = None   
superscript: bool = None  
bold: bool = False
italic: bool = False
underline: str = False  # options: `'single', 'double', 'thick', 'dotted', 'dash', 'dotDash', 'dotDotDash', 'wave'`
strike: bool = False
font: str = "Arial"
url_id: str = None  # e.g., `url_id=tpl.build_url_id("http://google.com")` where `tpl` is a `DocxTemplate` object



RT

 RT (_default_opts=None, text=None, **text_prop)

Inherits from base docxtpl RichText and adds a few QOL methods. When initializing, pass in RTFormatOpts only.



RT.addText

 RT.addText (text:str, **text_prop)

Add text and any additional styling options.




Type
Details




text
str
str


text_prop
VAR_KEYWORD



Returns
None






Example

def createSampleRT(tr: pd.Series) -> RichText:
    """-> RichText

    Parameters
    ----------
    tr : pd.Series
        pd.Series

    Returns
    -------
    RichText
        RichText
    """
    name = tr["name"]
    _id = tr["id"]
    group = tr["group"]

    _opts = RTFormatOpts(size=30)
    rt = RT(_opts)

    rt.addText("Member ID: ")
    rt.addText(_id, bold=True)
    rt.addText("\n")
    rt.addText("Name: ")
    rt.addText(name, bold=True, italic=True, underline="thick", color="#FF0000")
    rt.addText("\n")
    rt.addText("Group ", color="#32a856", bold=True)
    rt.addText(group, color="#32a856", bold=True)
    # rt.addText()

    return rt


df = pd.DataFrame(columns=["id", "group", "name"])
df.loc[0] = ["123", "A", "Bob"]
df["text"] = df.apply(createSampleRT, axis=1).astype(str)  # type: ignore

df.to_parquet("../tests/richtext/dat.parquet")

mmm.merge("../tests/richtext/cfg.yml")

Python’s built-in round function can return unexpected results. See https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#round. This function returns the same result as the Excel ROUND function.

testFixRound
with pytest.raises(Exception, match="invalid input"):
    fix_round("test", 123)  # type: ignore

assert round(23.335, 2) == 23.34
assert round(23.345, 2) == 23.34
assert fix_round(23.345, 2) == 23.35

assert round(-23.345, 2) == -23.34
assert fix_round(-23.345, 2) == -23.35

assert fix_round(1, 2) == 1
assert isinstance((fix_round(1, 2)), float)

assert fix_round(1.0, 2) == 1
assert isinstance((fix_round(1.0, 2)), float)

assert round(6789.2342335, 6) == 6789.234234
assert round(6789.2342345, 6) == 6789.234234
assert fix_round(6789.2342345, 6) == 6789.234235

assert round(-6789.2342345, 6) == -6789.234234
assert fix_round(-6789.2342345, 6) == -6789.234235

assert fix_round(0.0, 2) == 0.0
assert fix_round(-0.0, 2) == 0.0

# null input
assert fix_round(None, 5) == None
assert fix_round(np.nan, 5) == None
assert fix_round(pd.NaT, 5) == None  # type: ignore
assert fix_round(pd.NA, 5) == None  # type: ignore

testRoundAndFormat
assert round_and_format(123.445, 2, FormatOptions()) == "123.45"
assert round_and_format(9123.445, 2, FormatOptions()) == "9,123.45"
assert round_and_format(2123.445, 2, FormatOptions(comma_str="")) == "2123.45"
assert (
    round_and_format(123.445, 4, FormatOptions(comma_str="", pad_zeroes_at_end=True))
    == "123.4450"
)
assert round_and_format(-2342.475, 2, FormatOptions()) == "-2,342.48"

assert (
    round_and_format(2342.999, 0, FormatOptions(return_int_if_possible=True)) == "2,343"
)
assert (
    round_and_format(2342.999, 0, FormatOptions(return_int_if_possible=False))
    == "2,343.0"
)
assert (
    round_and_format(
        2342.999, 0, FormatOptions(return_int_if_possible=False, comma_str="")
    )
    == "2343.0"
)
assert round_and_format(2342.999, 0, FormatOptions(comma_str="")) == "2343.0"

assert (
    round_and_format(2342.999, 1, FormatOptions(return_int_if_possible=True)) == "2,343"
)
assert (
    round_and_format(
        2342.999, 1, FormatOptions(return_int_if_possible=True, comma_str="")
    )
    == "2343"
)
assert (
    round_and_format(2342.999, 1, FormatOptions(return_int_if_possible=False))
    == "2,343.0"
)

assert round_and_format(0.0, 0, FormatOptions()) == "0.0"

x = round_and_format(9123.445, 2, FormatOptions(_format=False))
assert isinstance(x, float)




testInvalidInputs
default_opts = FormatOptions()
with pytest.raises(Exception, match="Invalid input"):
    round_and_format("0", 0, default_opts)  # type: ignore
with pytest.raises(Exception, match="Invalid input"):
    round_and_format("abc", 0, default_opts)  # type: ignore

assert round_and_format("abc", 0, default_opts, "coerce") == None  # type: ignore
assert round_and_format("abc", 0, default_opts, "ignore") == "abc"  # type: ignore




testNullInput
x = round_and_format(None, 0, default_opts)  # type: ignore
assert x is None

x = round_and_format(np.nan, 0, default_opts)  # type: ignore
assert x is None

x = round_and_format(pd.NaT, 0, default_opts)  # type: ignore
assert x is None

x = round_and_format(pd.NA, 0, default_opts)  # type: ignore
assert x is None




testAccountingNotation
assert (
    round_and_format(
        -9123.56345, 2, FormatOptions(prefix="$", accounting_notation=True)
    )
    == "$(9,123.56)"
)
assert (
    round_and_format(9123.56345, 2, FormatOptions(prefix="$", accounting_notation=True))
    == "$9,123.56"
)
assert (
    round_and_format(
        -5.56123345,
        2,
        FormatOptions(comma_str="", suffix="%", accounting_notation=True),
    )
    == "(5.56)%"
)
assert (
    round_and_format(
        5.56123345,
        2,
        FormatOptions(comma_str=" ", suffix="%", accounting_notation=True),
    )
    == "5.56%"
)




testIgnoreNa
x = round_and_format(None, 2, FormatOptions(ignore_na=True))  # type: ignore
assert x is None

with pytest.raises(Exception, match="Invalid input"):
    x = round_and_format(None, 2, FormatOptions(ignore_na=False))  # type: ignore

assert (
    round_and_format(None, 2, FormatOptions(ignore_na=False), errors="coerce") == None
)
assert (
    round_and_format(None, 2, FormatOptions(ignore_na=False), errors="ignore") == None
)

testDateToStr
x = datetime(2024, 3, 19, 16, 39, 2, 126548)
assert date_to_string(x) == "March 19, 2024"
assert date_to_string(x, long=False) == "Mar 19, 2024"
assert date_to_string(x, period=True, long=False) == "Mar. 19, 2024"

x = pd.to_datetime("19-mar-2024")
assert date_to_string(x) == "March 19, 2024"
assert date_to_string(x, long=False) == "Mar 19, 2024"
assert date_to_string(x, period=True, long=False) == "Mar. 19, 2024"




testFrench
x = datetime(1920, 12, 1, 0, 0)
assert date_to_string(x, french=True) == "1 décembre 1920"
assert date_to_string(x, french=True, long=False, period=True) == "1 déc. 1920"
assert date_to_string(x, french=True, long=False, period=False) == "1 déc 1920"

x = pd.to_datetime("1-dec-1920")
assert date_to_string(x, french=True) == "1 décembre 1920"
assert date_to_string(x, french=True, long=False, period=True) == "1 déc. 1920"
assert date_to_string(x, french=True, long=False, period=False) == "1 déc 1920"




testInvalidAndNullInput
with pytest.raises(Exception, match="Invalid input"):
    date_to_string("19-mar-2024")  # type: ignore

with pytest.raises(Exception, match="Invalid input"):
    date_to_string(123)  # type: ignore
with pytest.raises(Exception, match="Invalid input"):
    date_to_string(0)  # type: ignore

assert date_to_string(123, errors="ignore") == 123  # type: ignore
assert date_to_string(123, errors="coerce") == None  # type: ignore

# null input
x = date_to_string(None)  # type: ignore
assert x is None
x = date_to_string(pd.NaT)  # type: ignore
assert x is None
x = date_to_string(pd.NA)  # type: ignore
assert x is None
x = date_to_string(np.nan)  # type: ignore
assert x is None

with pytest.raises(Exception, match="Invalid input"):
    date_to_string(None, ignore_na=False)  # type: ignore

assert date_to_string(None, ignore_na=False, errors="ignore") == None  # type: ignore
assert date_to_string(None, ignore_na=False, errors="coerce") == None  # type: ignore

assert round_and_format(2342.999, 0, FormatOptions(comma_str="")) == "2343.0"

assert (
    round_and_format(2342.999, 1, FormatOptions(return_int_if_possible=True)) == "2,343"
)
assert (
    round_and_format(
        2342.999, 1, FormatOptions(return_int_if_possible=True, comma_str="")
    )
    == "2343"
)
assert (
    round_and_format(2342.999, 1, FormatOptions(return_int_if_possible=False))
    == "2,343.0"
)

assert round_and_format(0.0, 0, FormatOptions()) == "0.0"

x = round_and_format(9123.445, 2, FormatOptions(_format=False))
assert isinstance(x, float)




testInvalidInputs
default_opts = FormatOptions()
with pytest.raises(Exception, match="Invalid input"):
    round_and_format("0", 0, default_opts)  # type: ignore
with pytest.raises(Exception, match="Invalid input"):
    round_and_format("abc", 0, default_opts)  # type: ignore

assert round_and_format("abc", 0, default_opts, "coerce") == None  # type: ignore
assert round_and_format("abc", 0, default_opts, "ignore") == "abc"  # type: ignore




testNullInput
x = round_and_format(None, 0, default_opts)  # type: ignore
assert x is None

x = round_and_format(np.nan, 0, default_opts)  # type: ignore
assert x is None

x = round_and_format(pd.NaT, 0, default_opts)  # type: ignore
assert x is None

x = round_and_format(pd.NA, 0, default_opts)  # type: ignore
assert x is None




testAccountingNotation
assert (
    round_and_format(
        -9123.56345, 2, FormatOptions(prefix="$", accounting_notation=True)
    )
    == "$(9,123.56)"
)
assert (
    round_and_format(9123.56345, 2, FormatOptions(prefix="$", accounting_notation=True))
    == "$9,123.56"
)
assert (
    round_and_format(
        -5.56123345,
        2,
        FormatOptions(comma_str="", suffix="%", accounting_notation=True),
    )
    == "(5.56)%"
)
assert (
    round_and_format(
        5.56123345,
        2,
        FormatOptions(comma_str=" ", suffix="%", accounting_notation=True),
    )
    == "5.56%"
)




testIgnoreNa
x = round_and_format(None, 2, FormatOptions(ignore_na=True))  # type: ignore
assert x is None

with pytest.raises(Exception, match="Invalid input"):
    x = round_and_format(None, 2, FormatOptions(ignore_na=False))  # type: ignore

assert (
    round_and_format(None, 2, FormatOptions(ignore_na=False), errors="coerce") == None
)
assert (
    round_and_format(None, 2, FormatOptions(ignore_na=False), errors="ignore") == None
)

The config file uses YAML format for easy editing. Here you specify the data / template filepaths, as well as which groups require which templates. For example:
data: 'C:\path\to\data.parquet'
id_col: 'id'
group_col: '_group'
multi_line_cols:  # optional
  - 'str_mailing_details'
tables:  # optional
  - 'tbl1'
  - 'tbl2'
groups: 
- group1:
  - 'C:\path\to\template.docx'
  - 'C:\path\to\template2.docx'
- group2:
  - 'C:\path\to\template.docx'
  - 'C:\path\to\template3.docx'
This is particularly useful when you have many groups, each requiring different combinations of templates.
